name: Republic of Belarus

areaKm2.note: asOf 2024: land area 202,976 km2 (AG.LND.TOTL.K2). Low/high allow for the Natural Earth polygon vs official figure and inland water (surface area is a few % larger).

population.note: asOf 2025: World Bank SP.POP.TOTL 9,085,991. Range allows for 2026 drift and census revisions.

activePersonnel.note: Armed Forces of Belarus article quoting IISS 2025: 48,600 active and 289,500 reserves (IISS 2026 p.180 on the personnel list gives the same active). High: CIA Factbook 2025 50-60,000.

trainedReserves.note: IISS as quoted: 289,500 reserves (men with conscript service within five years). Low for the share callable with equipment.

supportPersonnel.note: Active 48,600 minus infantry P roles (15,000). Covers navy and air force personnel, armour/artillery/air-defence crews, logistics, staff, training and other support.

mobilizationRatio.note: Analogy to Soviet-model mobilization scaled for a small conscript state with large Soviet-era equipment stocks.

count.note: Educated guess. 4 mechanized brigades (BMP-2/BTR-82A) x ~1,500 dismounts plus conscripts. commandQuality.note: Rubric commandQuality 0.5 (competent staff, average generalship) (slightly below): Soviet-model staff, dependent on Russian command integration; no combat experience.

cohesion.note: Rubric cohesion 0.5 (national conscript army): Conscript army of an authoritarian state.

morale.note: Rubric morale 0.5 (average) (slightly below): Low willingness to fight Ukraine or NATO (Belarus stayed out of the 2022 ground war).

weapons.note: Between anchor 8 and 9: Polonez MLRS, Iskander, Tor-M2; Soviet-era core.

fortification.note: Between anchor 8 and 9: Soviet-era fortified areas, S-400.

logistics.note: Between anchor 8 and 9: Rail-based, Russian supply.

isr.note: Between anchor 8 and 9: Limited UAVs, Russian ISR.

cyber.note: Between anchor 8 and 9: State cyber units (KGB/GUBOPiK).

gdpPerCapita.note: asOf 2025. GDP 215,772,318,543 2011 int$ (World Bank NY.GDP.MKTP.PP.KD x 0.8005) / population 9,085,991 = 23,748. Range +/-10%. Corrected 2026-10-29: values x1.0376 because the rebase factor was an arithmetic error (0.8005); the right factor is 0.8306 (FRED GDPDEF, 2017=100: 2011 91.478 / 2021 110.130). Figures quoted above are before the correction.

gdp.note: asOf 2025. World Bank NY.GDP.MKTP.PP.KD (constant 2021 int$) 269,546,931,346 x 0.8005 (US GDP deflator 2011/2021) = 215,772,318,543 2011 int$. Range +/-10% for PPP benchmark uncertainty and the relative-price drift the rebase ignores. Corrected 2026-10-29: values x1.0376 because the rebase factor was an arithmetic error (0.8005); the right factor is 0.8306 (FRED GDPDEF, 2017=100: 2011 91.478 / 2021 110.130). Figures quoted above are before the correction.

milSpendShare.note: SIPRI via World Bank MS.MIL.XPND.GD.ZS: 2.40% of GDP in 2025 (mid), 1.98% in 2024, 1.75% in 2021. Low is the lowest of those years; high allows ~5% for NATO-definition spending above SIPRI.

industrialShare.note: asOf 2025: industry incl. construction 31.6% of GDP (NV.IND.TOTL.ZS). Range +/-1.5 pp for year-to-year variation.

foodSurplus.note: Educated guess. Exporter of dairy and meat to Russia.

annualCohort.note: asOf 2025. Males reaching military age per year = male population 4,233,066 (SP.POP.TOTL.MA.IN) x share of males aged 15-19 6.221% (SP.POP.1519.MA.5Y) / 5 = 52,667. Males only (conscript-pool convention); about double if women are counted. Range +/-10%.

missiles.note: Educated guess. Polonez-M launchers built domestically on MZKT chassis. (context page: https://ru.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D0%A1%D1%83%D1%85%D0%BE%D0%BF%D1%83%D1%82%D0%BD%D1%8B%D0%B5_%D0%B2%D0%BE%D0%B9%D1%81%D0%BA%D0%B0_%D0%91%D0%B5%D0%BB%D0%BE%D1%80%D1%83%D1%81%D1%81%D0%B8%D0%B8)

ifv_apc.note: Educated guess. Overhaul plants (BTRZ); Kaiman light vehicles.

roadKm.note: Educated guess. Belarus is not in the fetched road-network table; ~86,000 km of public roads is the commonly cited order of magnitude. (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_countries_by_road_network_size)

railKm.note: asOf 2021: 5,474 route-km (IS.RRS.TOTL.KM). Low allows for closures since.

merchantTonnage.note: Educated guess. Landlocked; CIA Factbook lists 4 Belarus-flag vessels (2023, "other").

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess. Soviet-model rail-based logistics, depot-dependent.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess. Horses, mules and donkeys, not from FAO data. Militarily irrelevant in 2026.

nuclearWarheads.note: Non-nuclear-weapon state (NPT); FAS Status of World Nuclear Forces 2026 lists only nine nuclear-armed states. Russia stationed non-strategic nuclear weapons in Belarus from 2023 (FAS); they are under Russian control and counted for Russia, not here.

homeDefense.note: Rubric 1.1: familiar forested and marsh terrain; limited population support for a regime war.

notes: Modern snapshot, asOf 2025 World Bank data with an Oct 2026 order of battle. Population convention: everything inside ne:BLR. Money in 2011 int$ via derived:ppp-rebase-2011. Ground equipment from the Russian Wikipedia ground forces article quoting IISS Military Balance 2022, so counts are four years old (grade C); personnel from IISS 2025/2026 as quoted. Infantry P-role splits are educated guesses (grade D). Large Soviet-era equipment parks in storage, partly transferred to Russia since 2022, are excluded. Landlocked: ships tech is 0 with grade B (no navy).
